title: mTORC1 drives cell-autonomous astrocyte reactivity in tuberous sclerosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found GEO GSE341692 (single-cell RNA-seq, 40 samples, public since 5 Sep 2026) and GSE341690 (bulk RNA-seq, 18 samples) by searching GEO. Read the GEO series design text, which maps tdTomato-sorted fractions to TSC2 genotype. Listed all 40 per-sample 10x files (873 MB of gzipped count matrices in total; 846 MB tar). Downloaded one sample (GSM9915224): 814 cells x 36,601 Ensembl genes, 1.59M non-zero counts, made by cellranger 6.1.2. No tdTomato transcript in the gene list; TSC2 is present. Opened the bulk matrix: 35,719 genes x 18 columns (3 batches x 3 replicates x KO/WT); TSC2 counts are about 2,700 in KO versus about 8,000 in WT. Found that the genotyped patient FCD (focal cortical dysplasia) single-nucleus dataset (Baldassari 2025, Nature Neuroscience) is on EGA under controlled access.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: No full text was available (paywalled; no PMCID), so the cell-type annotations, the reactive-astrocyte signature, cell counts and the patient tuber cyclic-immunostaining results come from the abstract and GEO summary only. The total of about 92,000 cells is my estimate from barcode-file sizes, not a count. No cell-level metadata or annotation file is deposited.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO GSE341692 is public. I downloaded one sample's barcodes, features and matrix files individually without logging in.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The genotype label (TSC2 -/- vs +/-, or +/- vs +/+) is fixed per sample by FACS (fluorescence-activated cell sorting) on tdTomato and is encoded in each file name (C-/Cplus, Ctrl/tdTom), per the GEO design text. Cell-type labels such as 'reactive astrocyte' are NOT deposited and would have to be built by clustering, so the project uses genotype only.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full UMI (unique molecular identifier) count matrices with Ensembl gene IDs and symbols are present. I checked this in one sample.

a4_units_stated.note: Raw integer UMI counts from cellranger 6.1.2 (stated in the MatrixMarket file header). The bulk data is raw gene counts.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 92,000 cells, estimated from barcode-file sizes (814 cells counted in one sample). Only about 20 tdTom/Ctrl library pairs are independent units, so the effective sample size is batches, not cells.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.9 GB gzipped mtx; ~2-3 GB in memory as a sparse matrix
a6_fits_laptop.note: Estimated about 180M non-zero values in total (sparse storage, under 3 GB RAM). The baseline needs no GPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: I could not compare against the paper because the full text is unavailable. GEO's 40 samples match its own file list. Cell numbers per sample are not verified against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is an engineered genotype read out by FACS on a reporter, which is a physical measurement and not a model output. Leakage risk: TSC2 mRNA itself is lower in knockout cells (bulk: about 2,700 vs 8,000 counts), so TSC2 must be removed from the features. Each genotype is also its own 10x library, so library effects track the label.

B1.why: 40 per-sample 10x file triplets; sample metadata parsed from file names (verified file list).

B2.why: Standard 10x MatrixMarket files; one sample parsed first try.

B3.why: Raw counts across batches and two cell lines; needs normalisation and batch handling.

B4.why: Genotype labels are categorical; no censored values.

B5.why: Cellranger-filtered cells; doublets and ambient RNA (stray transcripts in droplets) still need removing; not checked.

B6.why: GEO design text explains genotype mapping; no cell-level annotation or QC (quality control) table deposited.

C1.why: Cross-line, cross-age transfer decay is always informative; the patient-tissue use case needs controlled-access validation data.

C2.why: No model found that predicts TSC2 second-hit status from single-cell expression; searches thin, so likely novel.

C3.why: Unique application: data nobody has modelled, used to learn a transferable 'second-hit cell' signature.

C4.why: Genotyping individual cells in patient lesions needs targeted single-cell genotyping, which is costly and covers few cells.

C5.why: No published ML number; dummy baselines are TSC2-expression-only and a marker-gene score.

D1.why: Geneformer and scGPT, single-cell foundation models, have open weights.

D2.why: Cell embeddings can be cached once on CPU; logistic-regression head on top.

D3.why: Geneformer Apache-2.0, scGPT MIT; GEO data public.

E1.why: Hold out whole batches, whole cell line (BJ vs WIBR3) or time point; all encoded in file names.

E2.why: BJ has 5 batches; WIBR3 has 3 batches x 2-3 days; about 20 library pairs.

E3.why: Majority class, TSC2-only classifier and published-marker score are computable.

E4.why: Replicate batches per line and day let between-batch agreement be measured; bulk has triplicates.

E5.why: Abstract's known effects: APOE, CLU up, glutamate transporters down, astrocyte bias in knockout cells.

E6.why: Label shuffle plus built-in C+ control (het vs wild-type sort) to expose sorting artefacts.

E7.why: Second stem-cell line (BJ) is an independent test; patient genotyped nuclei are controlled-access (EGA).

E8.why: No published model number; paper's cell-type proportions not seen (no full text).

G1.why: Ensembl gene IDs in every features file (verified).

G2.why: Genotyped FCD nuclei (Baldassari 2025) exist but are EGA controlled access; tuber snRNA-seq access unverified.

G3.why: Join is gene-space on Ensembl IDs, one-to-one.

G4.why: Combined question: does an organoid-learned TSC2-loss program find mutant cells in patient lesions?

H1.why: Both genotypes sorted from every organoid batch, plus a het-vs-wild-type background.

H2.why: Two stem-cell lines, one lab, organoids only, no seizures or immune cells.

H3.why: Claim can be stated precisely (see honest_claim_h3).

H4.why: Organoid limits explicit in abstract; one-library-per-genotype confound not stated.

I1.why: Bateup and Porter labs, FCD genotyping groups (Baulac lab), TSC Alliance.

I2.why: Could prioritise which patient cells to genotype; marginal unless it transfers.

I3.why: AUROC (area under the ROC curve) on held-out line roughly matches ranking cells for follow-up.

I4.why: A marker-gene score may match ML; that is the first thing to test.

J1.why: Grouped splits, foundation-model embeddings, cross-line transfer, leakage controls.

J2.why: Astrocyte markers give some intuition; neurobiology check needed.

J3.why: Even the C+ artefact check is a shareable finding on sort-confounded designs.

J4.why: About two weeks plausible; not formally set.

J5.why: Kill condition defined below; date not yet written in NOTES.md.

backbone.name: Geneformer (V1 small) or scGPT whole-human checkpoint, single-cell foundation models
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop; about 92k cells embedded once

integration.partner_dataset: Baldassari et al. 2025 (Nature Neuroscience) genotyped FCD type II single-nucleus RNA-seq, EGA EGAD50000001403 (controlled access); alternatively the open tuber snRNA-seq preprint (bioRxiv 2024.10.31.621014, access unverified)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a transcriptional program learned from engineered TSC2-null organoid cells identify naturally occurring mTOR-pathway second-hit cells in patient brain lesions?

controls.positive_control: Recover reported knockout effects (APOE and CLU up, SLC1A2/SLC1A3 glutamate transporters down) from model attributions; also check that an astrocyte-heavy shift appears in knockout fractions.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within batch. Classify the C+ line's tdTom+ vs tdTom- fractions (heterozygous vs wild-type): high accuracy there means sort or library artefacts. Drop TSC2 from the features.
controls.external_validation: Train on the WIBR3 line, test on the BJ line (independent genetic background, 5 batches). The patient genotyped nuclei are controlled-access on EGA.

honest_claim_h3: Within cortical organoids from two stem-cell lines, the model predicts whether a FACS-sorted cell is TSC2-null rather than heterozygous from its transcriptome, beyond what library and sorting effects explain; it says nothing yet about patient tissue.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression from brain organoids to predict which cells have lost both copies of the TSC2 gene.
plain_idea.train_on: About 92,000 organoid cells (an estimate from file sizes), each with expression counts for 36,601 genes, from 40 sorted libraries across two stem-cell lines, 5 ages and several batches.
plain_idea.predict: Whether each cell is TSC2-null or heterozygous. The truth comes from sorting cells on a red fluorescent reporter that marks the engineered second knockout.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tuber researchers can't easily tell which patient cells carry the second-hit mutation. A signature that transfers across stem-cell lines would show which cells to genotype. If it only learns sorting artefacts, that warns everyone who uses sorted-genotype single-cell designs.

label_elsewhere.sources: Baldassari et al. 2025 Nature Neuroscience genotyped mTOR-mutant FCD nuclei (EGA, controlled; read its data statement); PNAS 2025 cell-type-informed genotyping of mosaic focal epilepsies (seen in search, access not checked).
label_elsewhere.why: A few genotyped patient datasets could serve as external tests, but they are small and behind access applications.

risks: Each genotype is a separate 10x library, so ambient RNA, sequencing depth and sort-stress signatures track the label perfectly within a batch.
TSC2 mRNA is reduced in knockout cells (bulk 2,700 vs 8,000 counts), so the label leaks through the TSC2 gene itself.
Cells from the same organoid batch share culture effects; a random cell-level split puts sibling cells in train and test.
Cell-type composition differs by genotype (more astrocytes in knockouts), so a classifier may learn cell type rather than genotype.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole batches (Batch field in file names, seen), and as the main test train on WIBR3 and test on BJ (line field in file names, seen); report per time point.
checks: Run the same pipeline on C+ tdTom+ vs tdTom- (het vs wild-type): its AUROC sets the artefact floor that the knockout result must clearly beat.
Shuffle labels within batch and confirm AUROC around 0.5.
Classify within one cell type (e.g. astrocytes only) to remove the composition shortcut.
Train on library-level QC features alone (UMI count, mitochondrial fraction) and see how well they do.
leakage_plan.verdict: A serious risk, manageable only because the C+ heterozygous-vs-wild-type libraries provide a built-in artefact control.

success_criteria.metric: AUROC for TSC2-null vs heterozygous on the held-out BJ line, within astrocyte-lineage cells; it matches ranking cells for follow-up genotyping.
success_criteria.baselines: Majority class (0.5 AUROC); TSC2-expression-only classifier; marker score from the abstract's genes (APOE, CLU, GFAP, glutamate transporters); the same pipeline's AUROC on the C+ het-vs-wild-type artefact control. No published numbers exist.
success_criteria.success: Held-out-line AUROC at least 0.10 above both the marker-score baseline and the C+ artefact-control AUROC. These thresholds are pre-set by me; no data-derived number yet.
success_criteria.kill: If the C+ het-vs-wild-type AUROC is within 0.05 of the knockout-vs-het AUROC, or the marker score matches the model on BJ, stop after one week.

ambitious.why: Publishes biology-first ML on human cell models; it would need the signature to transfer to genotyped patient nuclei, which requires EGA access.

realistic.why: Fits a careful cross-line transfer study with explicit artefact controls in a sorted organoid design.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint plus NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics
fallback.why: A negative result showing sort-library artefacts dominate genotype classifiers is a publishable methods caution.

pitch.headline: 40 public single-cell libraries where each cell's TSC2 genotype is known from sorting, across two stem-cell lines and organoid ages from day 50 to 220.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Genotype is engineered and sorted, not inferred. A built-in heterozygous-vs-wild-type background (12 C+ libraries) gives a ready-made artefact control. Data released September 2026 with no ML on it found.
pitch.the_win: AUROC on held-out BJ-line cells at least 0.10 above both a marker-gene score and the het-vs-wild-type artefact control.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: It measures how much a sorted-genotype single-cell design lets library artefacts pass for genotype, which is a caution for mosaic-disease organoid studies.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Bateup lab (UC Berkeley) and FCD genotyping groups such as Baulac's (Paris Brain Institute), deciding which patient cells to target for genotyping.

ml_idea: Freeze Geneformer or scGPT and embed each organoid cell. Train a linear head to predict TSC2-null vs heterozygous status, excluding the TSC2 gene. Hold out whole batches and the BJ line, and benchmark against a marker-gene score and the C+ het-vs-wild-type artefact control.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed. RAM comes from about 180M non-zero values (extrapolated from one sample). Embedding time assumes 15-30 cells/s for Geneformer-small on CPU for 92k cells.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Load the C+ and C- libraries and run a logistic regression on log-normalised expression (without TSC2) holding out batch. If het-vs-wild-type is separated nearly as well as knockout-vs-het, the label is mostly library artefact.

verdict_reason: Public, laptop-sized single-cell data with a measured per-sample genotype label and no ML on it found. But genotype equals library, so the C+ het-vs-wild-type artefact check must come first, and the patient validation data is controlled-access.
